title: Kejriwal, Daughter Threatened in Call Demanding Rs 7 Crore in Bishnoi Gang's Name
excerpt: The threat reached AAP MLA Jarnail Singh, who complained to Mohali Police on November 6. A case is registered, but the caller's claimed gang link is unverified.
body:
• Former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal and his daughter Harshita have received a death threat from a caller who claimed to be a member of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang and demanded Rs 7 crore, according to the complaint reported by ANI.
  • The threat was not made to Kejriwal directly: AAP's Tilak Nagar MLA Jarnail Singh says he received the calls and WhatsApp messages on his phone and was asked to convey them.
  • Singh complained to the Mohali Senior Superintendent of Police on November 6; Mohali Police have registered a case under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the IT Act, and a cyber-crime team is examining call records and IP logs.
  • Police have not verified any gang connection: investigators are still establishing whether the caller belongs to the gang or used its name to spread fear.

Arvind Kejriwal, the former Delhi chief minister and Aam Aadmi Party national convener, and his daughter Harshita Kejriwal have been threatened with death by a caller who claimed to be a member of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang and demanded Rs 7 crore, according to a police complaint reported by ANI and India Today. Mohali Police in Punjab have registered a case and begun an investigation.

How the threat arrived

The calls were not made to Kejriwal himself. AAP's Tilak Nagar MLA Jarnail Singh has said he received threatening phone calls and WhatsApp messages from an unknown number, and that the sender asked him to convey the message to Kejriwal: pay Rs 7 crore, or Kejriwal and his daughter would be killed. Singh filed his complaint with the Mohali Senior Superintendent of Police on November 6 and also sought security for Kejriwal and his family, according to the ANI report carried by Daily Jagran.

The police investigation

Mohali Police have registered a case under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Information Technology Act. The investigation has been assigned to Inspector Sunil Kumar of the Cyber Crime Police Station, and officers are examining the suspect's call records, IP logs and location details, ANI reported. A more detailed account of the FIR, published by TezzBuzz, says screenshots of the threatening messages were handed to police as part of the complaint.

"Former Delhi Chief Minister and AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal has allegedly received a death threat in the name of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, with the sender demanding Rs 7 crore in extortion."

— ANI report, November 12

Claimed gang link is unverified

The Bishnoi connection rests, so far, entirely on the caller's own claim. Investigators are trying to establish whether the caller is actually associated with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang or used its name to spread fear, and whether other people are involved, according to the FIR reporting. The date of the threatening calls themselves has not been made public; what is known is the complaint date, November 6, and that the case became public on November 12.

Threats invoking the Bishnoi gang's name have become a recurring pattern in extortion cases reported across north India, which is precisely why police treat the claimed affiliation as a lead to be verified rather than a fact. For now, the verified position is narrow: a threat was made, a case is registered in Mohali, and a cyber-crime team is tracing the number behind it.
image_caption: Arvind Kejriwal addresses a press conference in front of an Aam Aadmi Party backdrop. Mohali Police have registered a case after a caller claiming Bishnoi gang membership demanded Rs 7 crore and threatened Kejriwal and his daughter.
nri_angle: Kejriwal leads the AAP, a party with deep support in Punjab and among the Punjabi diaspora; an extortion threat invoking the Bishnoi gang touches a diaspora community that follows Punjab security news closely.
author: Diaspora Desk
